A suitable recurrence, derived for this augmentation, uses λ = 2^(−1/4) ≈ 0.840896 and FP32 accumulators S=0, Z=0. Scan chronologically: for each real item xₜ, update S←λS+E(xₜ), Z←λZ+1, then emit pₜ=S/Z. Padding leaves both states unchanged and emits zero; empty prefixes return zero through a guarded denominator. This computes a normalized exponential pool without inverse powers or growing exponentials; Z remains bounded by 1/(1−λ). Include xₜ before predicting its next-item target, but never include that target. SASRec’s sampler explicitly pairs sequence[t] with positive[t]=the next interaction. Reset accumulators at the start of each retained, truncated window in both training and inference; carrying discarded history would define a different model. [Reference sampler](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/sampler.py).

Incorporate the pool inside the shared sequence-feature function, for example fₜ=hₜ+αWpₜ, with learned α and optional projection W. Train positive and negative logits as fₜ·E(candidate); inference uses the same feature computation and candidate embedding table, selecting the last valid position. This preserves SASRec’s shared dot-product scoring structure. Apply any normalization, scaling, or gating identically in both paths, and mask padded targets from loss. Update the predictor writer to reproduce the architecture and load α, W, and all other trained parameters. Check recurrence against explicit normalized decay weights, padding invariance, empty and truncated prefixes, and training/inference logits with dropout disabled. [Reference scoring implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py).
